quarterly_data.signal: 20-F supplier disclosure - Supplier Microsoft: SOPHiA's platform production environment currently runs on Microsoft Azure, which it uses for a substantial portion of its computing, storage, data processing and networking (it has ongoing R&D projects on AWS and Google Cloud Platform as well). Under its multi-year strategic partnership agreement with Microsoft, as amended effective November 1, 2022 and October 10, 2025, SOPHiA committed to buy products and services from the Microsoft Azure suite for an aggregate of approximately $80.9 million over a seven-year period ending October 31, 2029 (with a one-year grace period to October 31, 2030), in exchange for discounted pricing, a twelve-month Azure credit of approximately $1.8 million and approximately $1.3 million of Microsoft consulting and product support at no cost. Remaining commitments were $58.2 million as of December 31, 2025 ($56.9 million a year earlier). As of December 31, 2025 the platform architecture was deployed in 75 countries through its cloud-based solution; SOPHiA says it can deploy in a new geography in approximately one to four weeks if appropriate cloud infrastructure exists in Microsoft Azure, twelve weeks if it does not.
quarterly_data.figure: Azure minimum commitment approximately $80.9 million through October 31, 2029; $58.2 million remaining at December 31, 2025; platform deployed in 75 countries at December 31, 2025

quarterly_data.signal: 20-F supplier disclosure: SOPHiA relies on third parties for the manufacturing and supply of the products offered with its SOPHiA DDM Platform - a manufacturing and supply agreement with Integrated DNA Technologies (IDT, entered December 2015, amended and restated October 2018, amended March 2019) for commercial and research products, in particular DNA enrichment kits, under which IDT must ensure inventory and manufacturing capacity for SOPHiA's quarterly non-binding forecasts; an OEM supply agreement with Qiagen (January 2018) for amplification technologies; a supply agreement with New England Biolabs (January 2019) for reagents; and an OEM supply agreement with Watchmaker Genomics (December 2021) for components embedded in its library preparation kits.
quarterly_data.figure: four named supply agreements: IDT (December 2015), Qiagen (January 2018), New England Biolabs (January 2019), Watchmaker (December 2021)
